title: 7 Meal Templates You Can Build From Pantry Staples
description: Seven reusable dinner templates, bowls, pasta, soup, eggs, wraps, toast plates, and stews, for cooking from pantry staples you already have.
h1: 7 meal templates you can build from pantry staples
intro: A pantry dinner does not start with a perfect recipe. It starts with one useful question: what can this ingredient become if I give it a base, a sauce, and something fresh or crunchy?
That is usually enough to move from “there is nothing to eat” to a real dinner plan.

Most kitchens have more options than they look like they have. Pasta, rice, beans, lentils, eggs, tinned tomatoes, frozen vegetables, cheese, wraps, noodles, stock cubes, spices, and sauces can do a lot of work. The trick is not memorizing recipes. The trick is learning a few reliable combinations.

sections.heading: The pantry dinner formula
paragraphs: Use this simple structure when you are stuck:
You do not need every part to be fancy. You just need enough contrast for the meal to feel intentional.
steps: **Choose a base:** rice, pasta, noodles, couscous, potatoes, bread, wraps, or grains.
**Add something filling:** beans, lentils, chickpeas, eggs, tuna, cheese, tofu, chicken, or leftovers.
**Add vegetables:** fresh, frozen, roasted, tinned, or leftover cooked veg.
**Choose a sauce direction:** tomato, garlic and oil, curry, soy and sesame, lemon and herbs, yoghurt, pesto, or cheese.
**Finish with texture:** toasted breadcrumbs, seeds, nuts, crispy onions, salad leaves, pickles, or grated cheese.

sections.heading: Rice plus beans plus something sharp
paragraphs: Rice and beans can become a bowl, burrito filling, fried rice, or a quick stew. Add tinned tomatoes, spices, frozen corn, onion, or any leftover vegetables. Finish with yoghurt, hot sauce, lime, pickles, or grated cheese if you have them.

sections.heading: Pasta plus one sauce idea
paragraphs: Pasta is forgiving because almost anything can become the sauce. Tinned tomatoes with garlic, olive oil with chilli flakes, pesto with frozen peas, cream cheese with black pepper, or roasted vegetables blended with a splash of pasta water can all work.

sections.heading: Eggs plus whatever needs using
paragraphs: Eggs rescue small amounts of food. Leftover potatoes can become a tortilla. Soft vegetables can become a frittata. Rice can become egg fried rice. Bread can become eggs on toast with a quick tomato or bean topping.

sections.heading: Lentils plus stock plus vegetables
paragraphs: Lentils are one of the easiest pantry staples to turn into dinner. Simmer them with stock, tinned tomatoes, curry spices, carrots, onion, frozen spinach, or whatever vegetables are near the end of their life. Serve as soup, stew, dhal, or a bowl over rice.

sections.heading: Wraps plus leftovers
paragraphs: A wrap makes random ingredients feel like a meal. Add beans, eggs, chicken, roasted vegetables, cheese, salad, rice, or sauces. If the filling is soft, add something crunchy. If it is dry, add yoghurt, mayo, salsa, hummus, or dressing.

sections.heading: How to choose when you have too many random ingredients
paragraphs: Start with the ingredient that needs using first. That might be the half pepper, the open bag of spinach, the leftover rice, or the soft tomato. Then ask what format fits it best:
This keeps the meal practical and helps avoid food quietly expiring in the fridge.
list: Soft vegetables: soup, pasta sauce, frittata, curry.
Cooked rice: fried rice, bowls, stuffed wraps.
Beans or chickpeas: stew, salad, mash, wraps.
Cheese: pasta bake, toastie, omelette, quesadilla.
Bread: toast dinner, panzanella-style salad, breadcrumbs, eggy bread.

sections.heading: Try this tonight
paragraphs: Pick one base, one filling ingredient, and one sauce direction. If you have rice, chickpeas, frozen spinach, and tinned tomatoes, you already have the start of dinner.
